Home/IoT sensors/Water leak sensor

Wireless water leak sensor.The water event. The next step.

The Hitelecom H Series wireless water leakage sensor monitors for water reaching selected sensing locations around industrial equipment, utilities and critical spaces. Choose H200 for LoRa, H300 for 4G or H500 for NB-IoT; H300-WL002A is the specified 4G model. Match the sensing arrangement to the water source, expected flow path and installation, then define how events reach the receiving platform and the responsible team.

KEY FEATURES

A local water event.
A clear operational response.

Bring sensing locations, wireless coverage and the maintenance workflow into one installation plan.

Water-presence monitoring

Observe water reaching selected sensing locations near equipment, services and vulnerable assets.

Three wireless families

H200 uses LoRa, H300 uses 4G and H500 uses NB-IoT. Select the connection around site coverage and infrastructure.

H300-WL002A

A specified 4G model within the H Series water-leak family. Confirm the complete sensing and installation configuration for your project.

Installation-led coverage

Use likely leak sources and the path water follows to plan the sensing locations and required coverage.

Liquid-specific selection

Identify the water or condensate involved and any additives, contamination or cleaning conditions before choosing the sensing assembly.

A defined notification path

Agree event handling, responsible recipients and acknowledgement through the receiving monitoring system.

Industrial application planning

Build point layouts around pumps, cooling water, equipment trays, service routes and designated low points.

A serviceable installation

Plan access for inspection, controlled testing, cleaning and recovery checks throughout the operating period.

Start with the source.
Follow the water path.

DETECTION & INSTALLATION

Position the sensing element. Keep the complete installation accessible.

Trace possible releases from joints, seals, hoses, drains or collection trays to the proposed sensing position. Review floor slope, barriers, normal washdown and cleaning practices. Match the sensing assembly to the actual liquid and operating conditions; locate the transmitter and its connections within their approved conditions. Keep routes clear of damage and leave practical access for inspection. Use a controlled wet test and recovery check to verify each installed point and its complete notification path.

FROM WATER DETECTION TO SITE ACTION

Recognise the event.
Give your team a next step.

Agree what happens between water contacting the sensing element and a responsible person receiving an actionable event. Detection behaviour, wireless reporting, platform rules and recovery handling each contribute to the result. Commission the complete path under the network conditions at the actual mounting position.

01

Detect

The supplied sensing assembly responds to water reaching its monitored location. Verify the actual liquid and sensing position during commissioning.

02

Deliver

The selected H200, H300 or H500 connection carries the configured event to the agreed receiving system. Check message identity, time and connection behaviour.

03

Respond

The receiving workflow directs the event to the responsible team. Define acknowledgement, inspection, escalation and the check that returns the point to service.

COMMISSION THE COMPLETE PATHTest the event. Check the recovery.

Use the supplied instructions to test a controlled water event, the received message, the intended notification and any supported recovery indication. Record the measured end-to-end timing for the site. If a local warning or equipment action is required, include its interface and behaviour in the engineering scope and test it separately.

01Factory production equipment5 monitoring tasks +

Put water detection beside the connections that move, wear or get serviced: cooling circuits, flexible hoses, valves and equipment service bays. Match each sensing point to a practical inspection route.

Machine-tool cooling connections

Local presence of water or a confirmed compatible water-based coolant.+

Machine tools may have spindle cooling, water supply and water-based coolant circuits close to moving hoses and service connections. Place detection at a defined collection point outside the machining enclosure to identify unexpected liquid reaching that position. For coolant mixtures, confirm the actual formulation, contamination and sensing compatibility before selecting the configuration and arranging a representative site test.

What to detect
Local presence of water or a confirmed compatible water-based coolant.
Detection point
External cooling hose connections, service trays and floor collection points beside the machine.
Installation approach
Agree a mounting point clear of moving axes, hot surfaces and routine spray. Route and secure the sensing assembly so machine servicing remains practical, and validate detection with the actual approved fluid.
Specify for your project
Share the machine type, circuit fluid, likely collection point and routine cleaning method.
Discuss this application ↗

Injection-moulding cooling manifolds

Water reaching the selected cooling-manifold collection area.+

Mould cooling systems contain multiple supply and return connections that are disconnected or adjusted during tool changes. A defined detection position beneath an external manifold or hose service area can help the maintenance team investigate water that escapes during production. Separate normal tool-change drainage from unexpected wetness, and associate the alert with the machine and cooling zone concerned.

What to detect
Water reaching the selected cooling-manifold collection area.
Detection point
External mould-cooling manifolds, hose connection banks and approved drip-tray low points.
Installation approach
Position the approved sensing assembly outside the mould movement area and clear of hot tooling. Keep connection access available, protect exposed routing and test the chosen point under normal production and tool-change conditions.
Specify for your project
Tell us the manifold layout, tool-change drainage routine and number of machines or cooling zones.

Agree whether the project concerns unexpected standing water, a particular service connection or a dry boundary beside production, and include cleaning chemicals and hygiene requirements in selection.

What to detect
Water present at an agreed utility point expected to remain dry in normal operation.
Detection point
Approved water-treatment skid perimeters, dry service boundaries and connection-area collection trays.
Installation approach
Choose locations with production and hygiene personnel. Keep components clear of food-contact surfaces and cleaning traffic, confirm chemical and environmental compatibility, and agree how scheduled washdown is handled in the notification workflow.
Specify for your project
Tell us the water service, normal wet or dry state, washdown process and required hygiene restrictions.

Industrial laundry water-service zones

Compatible water reaching an agreed dry service-zone detection point.+

Industrial laundries combine washer connections, water supply manifolds and drain routes with frequent cleaning and material movement. A selected detection position can identify water entering a service area that should remain dry during normal operation. Check the expected water temperature and detergent residues before configuration, then define how staff distinguish an equipment-service event from planned washdown or an intentionally wet drainage area.

What to detect
Compatible water reaching an agreed dry service-zone detection point.
Detection point
External washer-service connections, water-manifold bases and approved dry-zone collection points.
Installation approach
Place the approved assembly outside hot discharge paths, laundry carts and moving machinery. Confirm fluid and cleaning compatibility, keep drain access unobstructed and test the selected point against normal operating and washdown conditions.
Specify for your project
Provide the washer layout, water temperature, detergent exposure and the dry service zones to monitor.

07Below-grade and building services5 monitoring tasks +

Low points, service penetrations and concealed pipe routes can carry water away from its source. Select accessible detection positions and name the area clearly in the inspection and response plan.

Basement plant and pump rooms

Water present at a selected basement plant-room floor point.+

Basement plant rooms can receive water from equipment connections, building penetrations or adjacent low-level spaces. Detection at a selected floor low point can identify local accumulation and direct an inspection to the relevant room. Review normal drainage and sump operation when mapping the points, and keep water-presence notification separate from pump control or continuous measurement of the sump's liquid level.

What to detect
Water present at a selected basement plant-room floor point.
Detection point
Approved floor low points, plant-room thresholds and external equipment collection areas.
Installation approach
Select a maintainable point using the room's floor gradient and normal drainage pattern. Keep the assembly clear of sump mechanisms and access routes, and confirm environmental conditions at the chosen detection position.

Share the basement layout, normal drainage arrangement, sump equipment and water-entry routes of concern.

Utility galleries and service corridors

Water reaching a selected gallery low point or service-route collection area.+

Service galleries can carry water away from a pipe joint through shared channels and floor gradients. A named detection point at an accessible low section can help maintenance staff identify where water has collected and plan their inspection. Divide long routes according to actual drainage boundaries and access points, with the sensing arrangement selected for each section rather than an assumed universal monitoring length.

What to detect
Water reaching a selected gallery low point or service-route collection area.
Detection point
Accessible channel low points, pipe-service collection areas and gallery drainage interfaces.

Use approved gallery access and working procedures. Keep sensing components clear of pipe supports, walking routes and drainage, and label the location so inspection teams can identify the correct section promptly.

Water reaching an approved collection point within the lift-pit installation area.+

Water may collect in a lift pit through building ingress, nearby services or drainage problems. A local detection position can be considered as part of an installation approved by the lift owner and maintenance provider. Define the pit access method, equipment clearances and response procedure before selection, with the lift's own controls and protective functions remaining under the responsible specialist's authority.

Water reaching an approved collection point within the lift-pit installation area.
Detection point
Lift-maintainer-approved pit low points or external collection positions identified in the site assessment.
Installation approach
Proceed only with the lift owner and maintenance provider's approval and access arrangements. Keep the assembly outside moving equipment and required clearances, using approved fixings and an agreed inspection and testing procedure.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently asked questions.

Practical answers for selecting water-detection points, choosing the connection and preparing a useful commissioning and response plan.

Ask about your project ↗
What does a wireless water leak sensor detect?+

It monitors for water reaching the installed sensing location and makes the detected condition available to a remote monitoring system through the selected wireless connection. Position the sensing element where leaked water is expected to reach it. The sensing construction and reported states are agreed for the supplied configuration.

How is water leak detection different from liquid-level measurement?+

Leak detection answers whether water has reached a selected monitoring point or sensing path. Continuous liquid-level measurement measures the height or depth of liquid in a tank or vessel. Choose the product by the operational question: unwanted water at a location, or an actual level value.

Which connection should I choose: LoRa, 4G or NB-IoT?+

Choose H200 for LoRa, H300 for 4G, or H500 for NB-IoT. Confirm radio coverage, the receiving infrastructure or network subscription, the destination platform and the required reporting behaviour at the planned installation. H300-WL002A is the 4G model specified for this page.

Where should a water leak sensor be installed in a factory?+

Start with likely leak sources, the route water will follow, and assets that need an early maintenance response. Typical positions include drip trays, pipe joints, pump bases, cooling skids and designated low points near equipment. Keep sensing surfaces accessible for inspection and apply the approved mounting and electrical-work rules.

Where does the two-pin point probe detect water?+

It detects water reaching the installed probe location. For several collection points, plan the sensing positions around the likely water paths and confirm the required number and arrangement of point probes. Discuss route or perimeter coverage as a separate sensing design.

Can the sensor be used for condensate, deionized water or process liquids?+

Select the sensing assembly for the actual liquid. Conductivity, contamination, temperature and contact materials can affect detection. For condensate, purified water, glycol mixtures or process liquids, confirm suitability with a representative liquid sample and the supplied configuration before rollout.

How should remote notifications be commissioned?+

Test the water alarm, received notification and any supported recovery indication according to the supplied instructions. Record the end-to-end timing under the site's network conditions.

Can water leak monitoring trigger a shut-off valve or machine action?+

If a shut-off or equipment response is needed, define it as part of the site control design. Confirm the required interface, power, control logic, fail-state behaviour and commissioning method. Agree this integration separately from the wireless monitoring function.

What should be checked during routine maintenance?+

Inspect the sensing surface and expected water path for dirt, damage, moved equipment or cleaning residues. Follow the supplied cleaning instructions and repeat a controlled detection and recovery check at intervals chosen for the environment and maintenance plan.

What information helps you configure a water leak monitoring project?+

Send the application, country, liquid type, likely leak points, coverage area, installation photos and quantity. Include the preferred H200 LoRa, H300 4G or H500 NB-IoT connection, platform destination, required notification path and any local control requirement. We can then review the sensing arrangement and project configuration.
